rows.text: Excavations documented four separate quarry tunnels 200–270 m east of the Sun Pyramid: Cueva de la Basura, de las Varillas, del Pirul, and del Camino. Deposits include roughly one metre of recent and Postclassic sediment over disintegrated tuff fill containing Teotihuacan pottery, slate and human remains; a scoria layer occurs in Cueva de la Basura.

The Cueva de la Basura assemblage includes mica, polychrome pottery, lithics, onyx pendants, cut/rounded human skulls and Prunus capuli seeds, with dates near AD 350–550 for some material. Sample Beta-69912 has an approximate calibrated average near AD 80, cautiously associated with possible extraction activity.

Thirteen burials were reported, including three seated adults facing south around a pillar and seven newborns in a central chamber beneath a ceiling opening. Vessels and projectile-point offerings accompanied burials; associated samples Beta-75377 and Beta-75381 averaged around AD 930.

The excavators recorded 13 circular storage-bin bases, seven around a burial area and six in an inner chamber approximately 50 metres from the entrance. Some contained Chenopodium, Amaranthus or maize remains. Figure 14 records sandal, foot and hand impressions in a leveled floor.

Fourteen burials included two seated adults, two flexed young adults, four children and six perinatal individuals. Three articulated dogs (two adults and a puppy) lay near child and newborn burials; two dogs are photographed near children in Figure 18. Distinct later Aztec activity dates near AD 1410–1435.

In Coyotlatelco contexts at Cueva del Pirul, the 2025 report identifies chenopod and maize macrobotanical remains in silo, hearth and burial contexts; amaranth in silos and burials; beans and purslane in silos; nopal/tuna and jaltomate in hearths and burials; chia in hearths.

For Mazapa contexts at Cueva del Pirul, the 2025 report identifies amaranth, chenopod, maize, jaltomate and purslane in hearths and burials, with Phaseolus limited to silo contexts and chia in hearths; its Aztec-period samples yielded maize, amaranth and chenopod in hearths.
More than 1680 sediment samples from quarry tunnels analyzed at UNAM 1994–1997

Chenopodium berlandieri achenes generally nondomesticated morphology; cultivation versus foraging unresolved
Coyotlatelco Varillas chenopods in silos hearths burials; maize amaranth purslane chia beans in silos/hearths but not burials
Two-sample KS maximum cumulative difference 0.26668 exceeds stated critical values 0.08023 and 0.11504

Sugiyama, Sugiyama and Sarabia describe a pre-main-pyramid wall approximately 2 m thick and more than 14 m long on a north–south axis, combining sloping talud and vertical faces; associated floors and Structure 1 were demolished as the large Sun Pyramid was built.

Offering 1 was placed in pyramid fill over the demolished earlier substructure and contained worked obsidian blades, projectile points and figurines, a pyrite disk, a large marine shell and organic fragments; excavators infer it was promptly covered during construction.

Offering 2 was recovered from a 1.75 × 1.75 m square pit cut to tepetate; published contents include 11 vessels with Tláloc effigies, two whole greenstone human figurines and a greenstone mask, worked obsidian, three pyrite-slate disks, a whole eagle containing two rabbits, and puma, wolf, condor and marine-shell remains.

Investigators report the main Sun Pyramid body as one principal construction phase, comprising layers of soil and pulverized tepetate mixed with stone, sherds, lithic material and charcoal, rather than large blocks or adobe; exposure of the west talud in Noguera's tunnel indicates the adosada platform was not part of the initial core.

The 1996 excavation report associates charcoal sample Beta-75379 (520 ± 60 radiocarbon years BP) with Cueva de las Varillas Burial 3 in Chamber 2, stratum 1k; Appendix Table 1 gives a late calendrical intercept of 1430 CE. The narrative calls the burial possibly Mazapa with Aztec intrusion. Consequently the 2025 Figure 2a Amaranthus specimen labeled Burial 3 cannot be assigned to Coyotlatelco solely from its caption.

Braswell reports Chicanel pottery mixed with Tzacualli sherds in Sun Pyramid fill, without Early Classic Maya polychromes dating after 150 CE in those contexts. Because fill ceramics are redeposited, the absence of Early Classic polychromes does not exclude later monument construction.

Braswell traces Xolalpan pottery in Kaminaljuyu Mounds A/B with Early Classic Maya polychromes, and in Tikal contexts associated with dated hieroglyphic inscriptions; he cites the 11 Eb' 15 Mak event of AD 378 as an anchor for a later pulse of Teotihuacan–Maya interaction. Redating earlier Miccaotli and Tlamimilolpa phases would affect these independent cross-ties.

Radiocarbon samples linked to Varillas Chamber 2 Burials 2 (Beta-75377, 1020±90 BP; 865–1220 CE), 3 (Beta-75379, 520±60 BP; 1310–1360/1380–1470 CE), 5 (Beta-75380, 1030±80 BP; 875–1195 CE), and 6 (Beta-75381, 1220±60 BP; 670–970 CE) are not one closely coeval group. Sample materials and direct burial association require further checking.

Pirul excavation register distinguishes Beta-90279 (Burial 15; 1540±70 BP, 2σ 395–650 CE), Beta-90280 (Burials 24/25/27; 1270±50 BP, 2σ 665–885 CE), Beta-90282 (Burial 27; 1170±50 BP, 2σ 770–990 CE), and Beta-90284 (above AA228; 560±60 BP, 2σ 1295–1450 CE). Dates span different contexts; avoid merging into one phase.

Excavation recorded an approximately 1m diameter clay circle with twined-pole impressions and compact earth floor with hand and foot impressions at approximately 0.675m depth, with ash, charcoal, jar fragments, figurine RT2006, metate fragment RT2099.
Below modern occupation layer, excavations found hearths with comales, Aztec III material, plates/jars, projectile points and grinding tools; a published 1280–1450 CE interval is tied to Beta-65547.

Burial 2 described as seated young adult woman older than roughly 22 years with slight cranial deformation, associated mica, obsidian, shell, greenstone/jadeite pieces and jadeite point RT1349; Aztec II–III material was identified as later intrusion.
